ElementDescription: The NDAR Global Unique Identifier (GUID) for research subject
Subject ID how it's defined in lab/project
Date on which the interview/genetic test/sampling/imaging/biospecimen was completed. MM/DD/YYYY
Age in months at the time of the interview/test/sampling/imaging.
Notes: Age is rounded to chronological month. If the research participant is 15-days-old at time of interview, the appropriate value would be 0 months. If the participant is 16-days-old, the value would be 1 month.

ElementDescription: Sex of subject at birth
Notes: M = Male; F = Female; O=Other; NR = Not reported

ElementDescription: Study participant diagnosis of interest
Notes: ADHD = Attention Deficit Hyperactivity disorder; TD = Typically Developing control

ElementDescription: Short interval cortical inhibition (SICI) pulse intensity for conditioning pulse (pre-pulse)
Notes: Expressed as ratio of resting motor threshold (RMT); typically less than 1.0

ElementDescription: Short interval cortical inhibition (SICI) pulse intensity for test pulse
Notes: Expressed as ratio of resting motor threshold (RMT); typically 1.0 or greater

ElementDescription: Short interval cortical inhibition (SICI) interstimulus interval in milliseconds (ms)
Notes: Time between paired pulses for SICI, typically 7 ms or less

ElementDescription: Intracortical facilitation (ICF) pulse intensity for conditioning pulse (pre-pulse)
Notes: Expressed as ratio of resting motor threshold (RMT); typically less than 1.0

ElementDescription: Intracortical facilitation (ICF) pulse intensity for test pulse
Notes: Expressed as ratio of resting motor threshold (RMT); typically 1.0 or more

ElementDescription: Intracortical facilitation (ICF) interstimulus interval
Notes: Time between paired pulses for ICF, typically 10 ms or more

ElementDescription: Cortical silent period pulse intensity
Notes: Expressed as ratio of active motor threshold (AMT); typically 1.0 or more

ElementDescription: Task related up modulation pulse intensity
Notes: Expressed as ratio of resting motor threshold (RMT); typically 1.0 or more
